title: Practice 4: Numerals, nouns and adjectives together

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: The film lasted 2 hours.
exercises.why: As we already know, the numerals «два», «три» and «четыре» in the Nominative case are followed by nouns in the Genitive singular, but the adjectives are in the Genitive plural. *Один он знает это. (= Только он знает это.) Он летал один. Я с ним в одном классе. Ни один человек не знает этого. Сколько книг вы прочитали? — Ни одной. Я познакомился с одним студентом, который знает вас.* Adjectives and possessives after numerals agree as a rule in number, gender and case with the noun they modify: *одна ваша новая машина; пять ваших новых машин.* However, there is an exception to this rule: after 2, 3, 4 (also after compounds ending in 2, 3, 4) the adjective or possessive is in the genitive plural, while the noun is in the genitive singular: *два наших самолёта; двадцать четыре новых самолёта.* — DLI, Lesson 70.  ·  «If the number ends in 2, 3 or 4 use the genitive singular … If the number ends in 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0 or -надцать use the genitive plural.» «There are also other quantity words that take the genitive, either singular or plural according to meaning: Много, Несколько, Мало, Сколько.» — Wikibooks, «Genitive case».
exercises.context: As we already know, the numerals «два», «три» and «четыре» in the Nominative case are followed by nouns in the Genitive singular, but the adjectives are in the Genitive plural.
